correctness.rationale: The basis-commutator formula identifies the subalgebra W, and D(e_{−x})=e_x−e_{−2x} makes D a graph incidence operator over Z and hence over every K. Spanning-tree differences prove free module images without divisibility assumptions. Functional components correspond bijectively to odd-component −2 orbits; each lies in a 3A-coset. Therefore the quotient is free rank c(O)−|A/3A|. If 3O=0 a telescoping integral right inverse exists; if 3O≠0 the zero coset contains a second orbit, making the quotient nonzero over every nonzero ring. All boundary cases are included. Two standalone independently implemented exact checkers corroborate cyclic 1..144 and 29 noncyclic/cyclic groups but are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The precise prior group-ring ideal theorem determines the span of commutators but neither the image of a single fixed-factor commutator operator nor the free orbit obstruction. The 2026 width tables cover finite fields only in bounded small orders. The new theorem proves fixed-factor surjectivity exactly for the full abelian two-primary-by-elementary-three class, uniformly over all nonzero commutative coefficient rings, with an explicit right inverse and sharp obstruction for every other finite abelian group. value.rationale: The work supplies a uniform single-commutator construction for a natural infinite family of core-quandle algebras over arbitrary coefficient rings, directly extending currently finite-field-focused commutator-width investigations. The orbit obstruction gives a sharp classification across every finite abelian underlying group and measures precisely why a universal fixed factor fails. It is not just a recomputation of previously established commutator subalgebras or small-field tables. No unrestricted-width classification is claimed outside the sharp fixed-factor family.
